q: Which language does the CPU execute directly?
options: A high-level language such as Python
Machine language made of binary 0s and 1s
explain: The CPU directly runs binary machine instructions; other languages must be translated into them.

q: Which CPU part decodes instructions and directs operations by issuing control signals?
explain: The Control Unit fetches and decodes instructions and coordinates registers, memory and I/O. It does not do the arithmetic itself.

q: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of the CPU?
explain: The three basic parts are the Control Unit, ALU and registers. A program unit is not a standard CPU component.

q: Which sequence correctly shows the instruction cycle?
explain: The CPU first fetches an instruction, decodes it, executes it, and writes back a result when needed.

q: Which of the following is NOT a stage of the instruction cycle?
explain: Device installation is not an instruction-cycle stage, although installation software also uses CPU cycles.

q: Which task is performed by the logic section of the ALU?
explain: Comparisons and Boolean operations (AND, OR, NOT) belong to the logic section. Addition and subtraction belong to the arithmetic section.

q: An accumulator is best described as:
options: A CPU register that holds an operand or an intermediate result
A separate kind of main memory
explain: An accumulator is a register used in some architectures; other designs store results in general-purpose registers.

q: Which statement about execution inside the CPU is accurate?
options: Every instruction is performed entirely by the ALU
The control unit performs all arithmetic
The ALU handles arithmetic and logic, while other execution units handle other instruction types
explain: Not every instruction is performed entirely by the ALU; a basic ALU may also lack hardware for functions like square roots, which may use an FPU or software.

q: Which register holds the address of the main-memory location to be read or written?
explain: MAR stores the address. MDR holds the data, PC the next instruction address and IR the current instruction.

q: Which register holds the address used to locate the next instruction?
explain: The Program Counter points to the next instruction, while the IR holds the instruction being decoded or executed.

q: MBR is another name for which register?
explain: MDR, also called MBR (Memory Buffer Register), holds data transferred to or from memory.

q: A register is usually built from which basic circuit element, with each element storing one bit?
explain: A register is a sequential digital circuit made from flip-flops, so an n-bit register holds n bits.

q: Among registers, cache and main memory, which is the fastest to access?
options: All three have the same speed
explain: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest; a hard disk or SSD is slower still.

q: What is the main purpose of a buffer?
options: To translate programs into machine code
To convert AC power to DC power
To temporarily hold data during transfer between components of different speeds
explain: A buffer smooths transfers when devices or components work at different rates.

q: Which statement about a stack is correct?
options: A stack is a way of organising data, not a separate memory technology with a fixed speed
A stack is a memory faster than registers
A stack is a type of hard disk
A stack is the same as cache memory
explain: A stack describes how data is organised, so it has no fixed speed of its own.

q: Clock speed of a CPU is measured in:
options: Hertz (Hz), such as MHz or GHz
explain: Clock frequency uses hertz. KIPS and MIPS measure instruction throughput, and bytes per second measure data transfer.

q: How is 1 MIPS related to KIPS?
explain: MIPS means million instructions per second, and KIPS means thousand instructions per second, so 1 MIPS equals 1,000 KIPS.

q: Which statement about CPU performance is correct?
options: Clock frequency alone does not decide performance
A higher GHz value always means a faster computer
Every instruction takes exactly one clock cycle
MIPS is a perfect comparison between all instruction sets
explain: Architecture, instructions per cycle, core count, cache, memory and workload also matter, and MIPS is not reliable across different instruction sets.

q: What does RISC stand for?
explain: RISC emphasises simpler, regular instruction designs and efficient execution.

q: Which statement about RISC and CISC is correct?
options: CISC is always cheaper to build than RISC
CISC supports more complex instruction forms; Arm is a RISC architecture family
Arm is a CISC architecture family
RISC and CISC describe the number of cores in a CPU
explain: RISC and CISC are instruction-set approaches; cost depends on the full implementation, and CISC is not automatically more costly.

q: How many cores does an octa-core processor have?
explain: Quad = 4, hexa = 6, octa = 8 and deca = 10 cores.

q: Which statement about a dual-core processor is correct?
options: It always belongs to the Intel Core 2 family
It has two separate physical CPUs
It has two cores and need not belong to the Intel Core 2 product family
explain: Dual-core describes the number of cores, not a brand name.

q: Which statement about CPU count and core count is correct?
options: One CPU package can contain several cores, so the two are different
A multi-core CPU is always a multiprocessor system
Multithreading means having multiple physical processors
A uniprocessor system always has a single core
explain: Physical CPU count and core count are different. Multithreading concerns execution threads, not physical processors.

q: The Intel 4004, introduced in 1971, was:
explain: It is widely recognised as the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor.

q: Microprocessor-based computers belong to which generation in the usual textbook classification?
explain: The fourth generation is the era of microprocessors.

q: How much physical memory can the Intel 8086 address with its 20-bit physical address?
explain: With 20 address bits it can address 2^20 bytes, which is 1,048,576 bytes or 1 MiB.

q: The name Intel was formed from which phrase?
explain: Intel comes from integrated electronics. AMD stands for Advanced Micro Devices.

q: ARM originally stood for:
explain: The Arm architecture originated at Acorn Computers; Advanced RISC Machine is a later, commonly taught expansion.

q: In which year did the ARM1 chip work?
explain: The ARM1 chip worked in 1985, with early use in Acorn computer systems.

q: What is the key strength of a GPU?
options: Replacing the control unit in every task
Handling many similar calculations in parallel
explain: A GPU was developed to speed up graphics rendering and is useful for other workloads that split into many similar calculations.

q: Which statement about a GPU and a graphics card is correct?
options: A graphics card is an add-in board that contains a GPU plus parts such as video memory and cooling
A GPU and a graphics card are exactly the same thing
A graphics card is a chip inside every CPU
An integrated GPU must always be on a separate graphics card
explain: The GPU is the chip; the card is the board around it. An integrated GPU need not be on a separate card.

q: Which statement about CPUs and GPUs is correct?
options: GPUs are always faster than CPUs
CPUs cannot do any parallel work
GPUs are not faster for every task, and CPUs can also perform parallel work
GPUs are used only for gaming
explain: CPUs handle general-purpose, control-heavy work, while GPUs excel at workloads that divide into similar calculations.

q: What does SMPS stand for?
explain: The power supply unit converts incoming AC electricity into regulated DC power for components.

q: Which statement about the computer cabinet is correct?
options: The assembled case and its contents are commonly called the system unit; CPU cabinet is an informal term
The cabinet is the same thing as the CPU
The cabinet contains only the processor
The system unit refers only to the monitor
explain: The CPU is just the processor, not the entire box that houses the motherboard, RAM, drives, power supply and cooling.

q: What does an offline device mean in traditional usage?
options: A device that is always faulty
A device that works only with the internet
A device built inside the CPU
A device unavailable for direct communication with or control by the computer
explain: An offline device may be disconnected or switched off; it is not necessarily faulty.

q: Which bus carries the address that identifies a memory location or device?
explain: The address bus says where; the data bus carries the data and instruction values; the control bus carries signals such as read and write.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three basic system buses?
explain: Address, data and control are the standard three categories; specialised cache interconnects exist but sit outside this basic classification.

q: Which company is associated with the GeForce 256, a major consumer GPU milestone of 1999?
explain: NVIDIA introduced the GeForce 256 in 1999. Sony is associated with the PlayStation graphics processor of 1994.
